title: Charlie Miller's band: Bill Lee, Driver and riffs behind the melody
summary: Solos were on chords, with Bill Lee on trumpet and Driver on trombone. Miller played only the melody on clarinet while the others faked three-part riff backgrounds.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: OK, some questions about that. When you say 'take solos', would they be solos the way we recognize jazz solos now? Were they melody reshapings or were they -
How many people in the band beside yourself were taking solos in this modern way?
The trumpeter was this man Lee, Bill Lee?
Right, and the trombonist was Dri -
Driver, which I can't think of his first name.
Well, I never did call his first name. (laughs)
Yeah, he only played the melody, only.

No, not at all. But he had a beautiful sound. I'll tell you the effect that he had on this instrument. It was like a violin playin' the melody. To tell you the truth, I think he played a C clarinet, and that case, he could play the violin parts. [ ] I'm sure he was playing a C clarinet. In that case he could play the violin parts, you know. And that's what he was taking the effect of, just the melody, never did - he didn't even make riffs. We were the ones that made it. For instance, he would play a melody on one of the songs back there that I remember real well now, a song called 'See You In My Dreams', you know (sings), was a very beautiful song. And he could play the melody real sweet, you know, just the melody. And we would make a background in riffs, and

most of the time we faked it, things like that. And the riffs that we were playing is similar to the things that you hearing today. [ ], three-part harmony - alto, trombone and trumpet. So he was just (sings), you know, one of those kind of things. And the, we could do that very fast, we could do it real easy because everybody had big ears, you know, they could hear, see. And I could fake it and Driver could fake it and the trumpet player could fake, and we had the right harmonies.
